core_obligations: The chain (1) => (2) => (7) => (1): geometric reducedness passes to every base change; reducedness of X_{k'} for all k' makes O(U) tensor_k k' reduced for affine open U, i.e. O(U) geometrically reduced; and conversely reducedness of all O(U) tensor_k k' glues to reducedness of X_{k'} (proof lines 436-453).

Reduce the remaining conditions to ring theory: having proved (1), (2), (7) equivalent, apply the algebra statement on finite purely inseparable extensions to the rings O_X(U) for affine open U, which identifies (1) with the conditions stated in terms of k^{1/p}, k^{perf} and kbar (proof lines 456-459).

Note the shape of the argument: the proof is a cycle of three implications plus one algebraic reduction, so no condition is proved in isolation and the reader has to keep track of which direction is being established at each step.
proof_roadmap: Show (1) => (2) by applying geometric reducedness to the local rings at points of the base change (proof lines 436-438).
Show (2) => (7) by restricting to an affine open and reading reducedness of Spec(O(U) tensor_k k') as reducedness of the ring (proof lines 440-446).

Show (7) => (1) by gluing the spectra of O_X(U) tensor_k k' to get X_{k'} (proof lines 448-453), and finally use the algebra lemma on finite purely inseparable extensions to bring in (3)-(6) (proof lines 455-459).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives seven equivalent formulations of geometric reducedness for a scheme X over a field of positive characteristic: via arbitrary base change, via finite purely inseparable extensions, via the two distinguished extensions k^{1/p} and k^{perf}, via the algebraic closure, and via the rings of affine opens (statement lines 419-432). The proof is a cycle (1) => (2) => (7) => (1) closing three genuinely different arguments — local rings on a base change, Spec of a tensor product, and gluing of spectra — and the remaining conditions are then attached by one algebraic statement applied to the rings O_X(U) (proof lines 436-459). What a reader cannot do routinely is see that the three directions are enough, i.e. that the cycle is closed and that the purely inseparable conditions follow from the same algebra lemma. The claim is H2.
